text: Why does RFC 3021 permit /31 on point-to-point links?
choices: There is exactly one possible recipient, so no broadcast address is needed and both addresses are usable
explanation: The usual -2 removes the network and broadcast addresses, which would leave a /31 with zero usable hosts. On a link with one peer, broadcast is meaningless. Using /31 instead of /30 halves the address consumption of router interconnects across a large network.
